learning_outcomes.text: Students become acquainted with ontologies, with their role in data representation and sharing, with ontological representation and query languages, and with ontology engineering methodologies.

They will also get acquainted with Semantic Web standards and with the principles and possibilities of publishing data in the Linked Open Data network, as well as the use of such data in knowledge-based applications.

syllabus_topics: Ontological representation languages (RDF, RDF Schema, OWL)
assessment_rules: Minimum passing requirements are 50% from the semester components (project, ongoing work) and 50% from the exam. The indicative assessment scale is A 90%, B 80%, C 70%, D 60%, E 50%. The scale of assessment (preliminary/final) is 80/20.
bibliography: Staab, S. and Studer, R. eds., 2010. Handbook on ontologies. Springer Science & Business Media.
Allemang, D. and Hendler, J., 2011. Semantic web for the working ontologist: effective modeling in RDFS and OWL. Elsevier.
institution: Univerzita Komenského v Bratislave (Comenius University Bratislava)
degree: Bachelor Applied Informatics (1-AIN), Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Informatics
